target_vertical: Multi-channel retailer, wholesaler/B2B distributor, light manufacturer, e-commerce seller
pricing_model: Tiered SaaS subscription with per-plan caps on users, orders/month, and integrations; paid add-ons (BOM/work orders, API access, additional users, Showroom Pro). 20% discount for annual billing.
starting_price_usd: $110/month (Entrepreneur tier, billed annually); $186/mo as the commonly-cited TrustRadius figure for monthly billing
free_trial_or_freemium: 14-day free trial (no credit card required); no permanent free tier
shopify_app_rating: ~1.3 / 5 (Shopify App Store, historically low; predominantly negative reviews)
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional for products and stock levels (after 2024/2025 updates); orders flow Shopify -> inFlow; fulfillments and stock updates flow inFlow -> Shopify. Prices can optionally be pushed inFlow -> Shopify.
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants (via SKU match), inventory/stock levels, orders, customers, fulfillments (tracking numbers pushed back to Shopify), prices (optional). Refunds and draft orders are not first-class synced entities. [uncertain on refunds/draft orders]
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — inFlow is a stocked-item-centric platform; non-physical/service items are not a documented first-class sync entity (unlike Katana's 2025 service-item release).
shopify_multi_store_support: Supported on higher tiers (multiple Shopify stores can connect to one inFlow tenant); subject to integration limits in each plan
shopify_pos_support: No native Shopify POS integration; inFlow has its own POS-style Sales/Showroom flow and Smart Scanner hardware. [uncertain on POS-specific sync]
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: [uncertain] — no public documentation of native handling of Shopify B2B catalogs/company locations/price lists; inFlow positions its own Showroom as the B2B portal
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — no documented native handling of Shopify Markets (multi-market pricing, duties, landed cost)
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: [uncertain] — no documented generic metafield <-> inFlow custom field mapping (Brightpearl-style)
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants mapped via SKU; each Shopify variant becomes/links to a distinct inFlow product. Products without matching SKUs can be auto-created in inFlow on first sync.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Webhook-driven / near real-time for orders; periodic sync for product/stock updates (community reports occasional delays and the need to manually trigger syncs on edits)
shopify_known_limitations: Historically very low Shopify App Store rating (~1.3 stars) with complaints of: (1) needing to duplicate product/customer/vendor edits across both systems prior to the 2024/2025 update; (2) tax/rounding adjustment lines being inserted that blocked fulfillment; (3) limited automation requiring manual intervention; (4) sluggish support response. inFlow has acknowledged these and shipped reduced-duplication updates.
etsy_supported: Third-party (via Extensiv Integration Manager / CartRover and Zapier; not a direct native Etsy API integration)
etsy_native_or_third_party: Third-party — routed through Extensiv Integration Manager (formerly CartRover) or Zapier; no direct first-party Etsy connector
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Sync-only (no creation of new Etsy listings from inFlow). [uncertain — exact capabilities depend on Extensiv/CartRover middleware]
etsy_inventory_sync: Stock pushed from inFlow to Etsy via Extensiv Integration Manager; frequency and depth depend on the middleware (typically near real-time for orders, scheduled for stock). [uncertain on specifics]
etsy_order_import: Orders pulled from Etsy into inFlow via Extensiv Integration Manager / CartRover (scheduled / near real-time) or Zapier
etsy_synced_entities: Listings (read), inventory (push), orders (pull), shipments (push tracking back). [uncertain — depends on middleware]
etsy_known_limitations: Not native; requires paid middleware (Extensiv Integration Manager) or Zapier; no native handling of Etsy variations, personalization fields, or digital products documented. [uncertain]
amazon_marketplaces: US, Canada, Mexico, UK, EU (DE, FR, IT, ES), Australia, Japan supported via the Amazon connector. [uncertain on full marketplace list]
amazon_seller_types: FBM (Seller Fulfilled) and FBA both supported for order import and stock sync; Vendor Central not supported.
amazon_synced_entities: Listings (via SKU match), inventory/stock levels, orders. Settlements, returns, and customer messaging are not first-class synced entities. [uncertain on returns]
amazon_listing_creation: Sync-only — inFlow matches existing Amazon listings by SKU; it does not create new Amazon listings.
amazon_repricing_support: Not included natively; would require a third-party repricer
amazon_buy_shipping: Not supported — inFlow ships labels through EasyPost integration, not Amazon Buy Shipping
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: [uncertain] — no public documentation of an FBA inbound shipment creation flow inside inFlow; FBA orders are pulled in but inbound shipment creation is not a documented feature
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — no public statement on migration to the Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20 API
amazon_settlement_report_handling: [uncertain] — no documented native processing of Amazon settlement reports into QuickBooks/Xero; typically users layer A2X or similar for this
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: [uncertain] — no documented native handling of Amazon marketplace-collected tax journaling
amazon_multi_account_support: Supported (multiple Amazon stores can be connected, subject to plan integration limits). [uncertain on hard cap]
amazon_known_limitations: Limited to operational sync (orders + inventory); accounting nuances (settlements, marketplace facilitator tax, FBA reimbursements) are not natively handled. No repricer, no Buy Shipping, no Vendor Central.
xero_supported: Native (first-party integration, listed on Xero App Store)
xero_app_store_certified: Listed on Xero App Store. [uncertain on specific certification badges]
xero_app_awards_recognition: [uncertain] — no documented Xero Global App Award recognition
xero_synced_entities: Sales invoices (from inFlow sales orders marked invoiced), bills (from purchase orders fully or partially received), payments (limited), contacts (customers and vendors auto-created), inventory asset value, COGS totals. Credit notes and granular inventory adjustment journals are not documented.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order — each inFlow sales order pushes as a discrete Xero invoice; each PO pushes as a discrete Xero bill; not a summary journal model like A2X
xero_cogs_journal_method: periodic_journal — total inventory asset value and total COGS are pushed (not a perpetual per-movement journal entry per shipment). Cost layers in inFlow use moving average / FIFO / LIFO at the inFlow side.
xero_multi_currency: Supported, but the base currency in inFlow and Xero must match; non-base currencies used on orders must be activated in Xero Settings or the order will fail to push
xero_tracking_category_mapping: [uncertain] — no documented mapping of inFlow locations/categories to Xero tracking categories
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes mapped at sync; products require SKUs (used as Item Codes on Xero invoices/bills). [uncertain on detailed GST/VAT mapping rules]
xero_known_limitations: One-way sync (inFlow -> Xero) — inFlow is the source of truth; no pull-back of edits made in Xero. Currency activation friction. Only totals (not detailed movement-level journals) for COGS/inventory value. No documented Xero tracking-category mapping.
qb_online_supported: Yes — native first-party QuickBooks Online integration (listed on Intuit App Store)
qb_desktop_supported: No — QuickBooks Desktop is not supported by the cloud product; only manual export workflows
qb_app_certified: Listed on Intuit App Store. [uncertain on QuickBooks 'App of the Year' or similar certifications]
qb_synced_entities: Sales orders -> QBO invoices (when marked invoiced), purchase orders -> QBO bills (on receipt), payments (two-way payment sync supported), customers and vendors (auto-created if missing), total inventory asset value, total COGS
qb_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order with two-way payment sync; not a summary journal
qb_cogs_journal_method: periodic_journal — totals for inventory value and COGS are pushed; cost calculations (moving average / FIFO / LIFO) happen inside inFlow
qb_multi_currency: Supported with the same base-currency-must-match constraint as Xero. [uncertain on full multi-currency depth]
qb_class_location_mapping: [uncertain] — no documented mapping to QBO Class or Location dimensions
qb_known_limitations: Push-only for invoices/bills; only totals for inventory value/COGS (no per-movement journal); no QuickBooks Desktop support; no documented Class/Location mapping; payment sync is the only two-way component.
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce (native), Amazon (native), Shopify (native), Squarespace (native). Via Extensiv Integration Manager (CartRover) and Zapier: eBay, Walmart, Etsy, BigCommerce, Magento 2, TikTok Shop and 35+ other carts/marketplaces. inFlow claims 95+ total integrations.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — inFlow supports assemblies/kits with BOMs; selling a kit/assembly decrements components (and disassembly increments components back). Multi-level (nested) BOMs supported.
other_accounting_integrations: QuickBooks Online and Xero are the only first-party accounting integrations. No native Sage, MYOB, Zoho Books, FreshBooks, NetSuite, or Wave integrations; users would rely on the inFlow REST API, Zapier, or CSV exports for those.
bom_support: Yes — Bill of Materials is a core feature (paid add-on $39-299/mo depending on plan tier)
multi_level_bom: Yes — supports nested sub-assemblies inside other BOMs for multi-level builds
production_orders: Yes — 'Manufacture Orders' (formerly Work Orders); stock availability checks, starring/pinning, customizable columns, disassembly, and operations/routings with labor cost tracking via the Production Management add-on (rolls labor cost into finished-good cost on completion)
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — lot number and expiry date tracking (released in beta during 2024/2025); supports end-to-end traceability
serial_tracking: Yes — serial number tracking with expiry/warranty period support per unit, scanned consistently across receiving, picking, and sale
bin_location_support: Yes — sublocations represent shelves, aisles, or bins within a physical location/warehouse
multi_warehouse: Yes — unlimited locations (subject to plan limits); each location can have sublocations
barcoding: Yes — supports existing UPC/EAN and can auto-generate internal barcodes; integrated label design and printing; USB and mobile camera scanners supported; first-party inFlow Smart Scanner hardware available
purchase_orders: Yes — PO creation, partial receipts, approval workflows with approver limits, supplier price tracking, cost methods (moving average / FIFO / LIFO) updated on receipt
supplier_management: Yes — vendor records with contact info; supplier-SKU mapping and pricing on POs. [uncertain on first-class lead time and MOQ fields]
landed_cost_support: [uncertain] — inFlow tracks unit cost via moving average/FIFO/LIFO and 'extra costs' can be added to POs; not clearly marketed as full landed-cost (freight/duty/insurance) allocation
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Single base currency for inventory valuation; multi-currency is supported on transactions (orders/POs) but valuation is in the base currency. [uncertain]
ai_demand_forecasting: Basic — inFlow markets 'AI reorder recommendations' and dynamic reports in 2025; deeper demand forecasting typically requires third-party StockTrim integration
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — AI-powered reorder/PO suggestions surfaced as a 2025 strategic focus alongside the B2B Showroom upgrade
ai_natural_language_query: [uncertain] — no public documentation of a chat-style 'ask your inventory' feature
public_api: Yes — REST + JSON public API documented at cloudapi.inflowinventory.com/docs; covers reads/writes across products, orders, customers, vendors, stock. Available as a paid add-on ($29-69/mo)
webhook_event_coverage: Outbound webhooks for product events (productCreated, productUpdated) and order/stock changes (per Zapier triggers: New Order, Updated Product, Stock Level Changes). [uncertain on full event catalog]
integration_architecture: Hybrid — first-party native connectors for Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, Squarespace, QuickBooks Online, Xero, EasyPost; partner-built iPaaS (Extensiv Integration Manager / CartRover) for Etsy, eBay, Walmart, BigCommerce, Magento, TikTok Shop, and 35+ others; Zapier for general automation
zapier_make_support: Zapier supported (official inFlow Zapier app with triggers and actions). Make/n8n not officially listed but reachable via the REST API. [uncertain on Make]
mobile_app: Yes — native iOS and Android companion apps for inFlow Cloud: create sales/purchase orders, stock in/out, transfers, picking, label printing, full inventory operations on the go
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — mobile apps use the device camera as a barcode scanner; first-party inFlow Smart Scanner is a rugged Android device with built-in laser scanner sold by Archon Systems
rate_limit_handling_documented: [uncertain] — inFlow's own API documents standard rate-limiting practices; no public deep documentation of how their connectors handle Shopify/Amazon/Xero/QBO throttles
sync_frequency: Real-time / webhook-driven for new orders across e-commerce connectors; periodic (typically every few minutes to ~15 min) for stock and product updates; Xero/QBO push on order state changes (invoiced, received). Exact cadences not publicly tabulated. [uncertain]
shipping_carrier_integrations: 100+ carriers via EasyPost (USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, Canada Post, Royal Mail, AusPost, etc.); rate shopping inside inFlow
shipping_label_buying: Yes — buy and print shipping labels directly inside inFlow via EasyPost (free up to ~36,000 labels/year, then EasyPost fees apply)
three_pl_integrations: Via Extensiv ecosystem (3PL Warehouse Manager) and Zapier; no first-party ShipBob/ShipHero/Deliverr connectors documented. [uncertain]
edi_support: Via Extensiv Integration Manager (which provides EDI for wholesale/retail partners); not natively built into inFlow
notable_customers: Over 40,000 small-to-mid businesses; downloaded by 1M+ users worldwide. inFlow publishes customer stories on its testimonials page across retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, and wholesale, but no marquee enterprise logos. [uncertain on specific named customers]
last_major_release: 2025 — AI-powered reorder suggestions and an upgraded B2B Showroom (branded catalog, real-time inventory visibility, custom pricing, abandoned-cart flows in Showroom Pro). Lot number + expiry date tracking shipped to beta in the same window. Additional updates released across April, May, and June 2025.
owner_parent_company: Archon Systems Inc. (private, Toronto-based; inFlow is Archon's flagship product, released 2007)
last_funding_event: Undisclosed growth investment from Delta-v Capital (date not publicly stated). [uncertain on exact date and amount]
public_status_page_uptime: [uncertain] — no widely-publicized public status page URL found
